doc.title: Toots Thielemans — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

chapter: Bebop and the first American trip
title: Members of the Belgian quintet and Armstrong missed
summary: He lists the vibraphonist, Jacques Pelzer and Jaspar, and notes he did not meet Armstrong until later.

story.theme_name: Who was in the band: naming sidemen and personnel
story.community_name: Who played in the band: reciting personnel

blocks.x: Who else was in the Belgian, your group? Bobby Jasper, yourself.

And a good vibraphone player. He died. Uh… [Savie Larlamans?]. And he was really Hampton, a little more articulate harmonically. But he was a showman and a combination Fats Waller and Lionel Hampton, you know.

But he had this place he played a lot in Paris, but he never really came to the States. Then that was [inaudible]. Oh, and Jacques [Belzer?], the alto player who played a lot later on with Chet Baker.
So two saxophone, vibes, and guitar, harmonica?
There was a pianist, I forgot. No, not so, not so easy to remember. [laughs]
So it was a pretty big group.
Yeah, it was a quintet, you know, but…
We didn’t really break it up. [laughs] And that’s when Louie Armstrong… I did that was… I didn’t go over to shake hands. That happened later.
